chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

A man from his companions entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and complained to him about another man from his companions. He did not wait long before the complained-about man arrived, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'What is it that your companion so-and-so is complaining about you?'
He said to him: 'They complain about me because I had my right adjudicated (went to court to claim my debt).'
So he said, and he sat in anger, and said: 'It seems that when you have your right adjudicated, you have not done poorly.'
Do you see what God the Exalted has narrated about you, saying: 'And they fear the evil of the Reckoning?'

They only feared that God would be unjust to them. By God, they did not fear except the act of having one's right adjudicated (al-istiqda'), so God named it 'the evil of the Reckling'. So whoever has his right adjudicated has done poorly.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.أَسَاءَ: Did poorly or committed a fault (opposite of ihsan).
key_terms.الاسْتِقْضَاءُ: The act of having one's right adjudicated in a court of law or by a judge.
key_terms.سُوءَ الْحِسَابِ: The evil or bad outcome of the Reckoning on the Day of Judgment.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on going to court to claim a debt according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the practice of *istiqda'* (seeking judicial adjudication) by linking it to the Quranic phrase 'fearing the evil of the Reckoning' (39:15). He interprets this fear not as general accountability, but specifically as the spiritual risk incurred when one resorts to secular courts to claim rights, thereby implying a subtle deficiency in trusting divine justice or fearing human judgment over God's. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *istiqda'* as a disliked act that, while not necessarily invalidating the right, carries a spiritual cost due to the potential for injustice or loss of merit.
